text:
anya: quick heads-up 1: we saw a production tenant with differing auth behaviour across hosting modes. hosted adapter silently removed the `x-rw-subtoken`, dedicated forwarded it, private sidecar returned 403 for the same request.

derek: oof. is it header normalization or policy enforcement?

anya: looks like both. hosted's proxy strips unknown x-* headers; dedicated proxy has an allowlist; private sidecar enforces stricter origin check.

tess: this will break any rollout that relies on transparent header passthrough. we need a single contract.

sam: proposal: introduce an "adapter-intent" contract header and a small capability handshake. controlplane sets `X-Redwood-Intent: prefer-forward|strip-if-unknown|require-origin` and adapters declare support via probe.

derek: i like the explicitness. we should also formalize a fallback policy: if adapter doesn't advertise intent capability, default to `strip-if-unknown` and emit a tenant-warning.

anya: +1. For private customers, add a compatibility flag in tenant manifest so operators can opt-in to stricter checks during scheduled maintenance.

tess: can we do a tiny example so infra can implement quickly?

anya: sample header chain:
```
X-Redwood-Intent: prefer-forward
X-Redwood-Policy-Version: 2025-01-12
X-Redwood-Preferred-Variant: gptx-8k:fused
```
Adapters respond to probe `GET /.well-known/redwood/adapter` -> `{"intent_support":"prefer-forward"}` (probe non-blocking).

sam: note: agents.md style option: the probe must be idempotent and read-only. controlplane does an async sweep and records `adapter_intent` on tenant manifest.

derek: alerts: if manifest requires `require-origin` and adapter reports `prefer-forward`, flag as `compat-mismatch` in console and block full rollout.

infra-bot: alert: compat-mismatch tenant=globex mode=private count=12 window=10m

tess: runbook suggestion: verify tenant manifest -> call probe endpoint -> if probe absent mark `legacy-adapter` and block until operator confirms. If probe returns incompatible, contact customer to schedule adapter upgrade or enable manifest compatibility shim.

sam: implementation checklist:
- controlplane: emit X-Redwood-Intent + policy version
- adapters: implement /.well-known/redwood/adapter (non-blocking)
- console: surface compat-mismatch and block hard-rollout when required
- ops: add compat-mismatch alert with clear escalation path

derek: edge cases: what about proxies that rewrite headers for security (e.g., strip all x-*). We should add a passthrough-exception header that asks upstream proxy to preserve X-Redwood-* headers when present. Might require infra support.

anya: agree. quick mitigation: have controlplane include a short-lived signed header `X-Redwood-Sig` so downstream proxies can validate and won't drop it. longer term, document header preservation requirements for on-prem installs.

deploy-bot: rollout: router-intent-v1 -> canary 5%

infra-bot: info: canary-report: 0.6% error increase in private mode, investigating

tess: ok, sounds actionable. i'll draft the tiny RFC (adapter-intent + probe) and include sample probe schema, sig header spec, and runbook.

derek: i'll own the alert rule + console blocker.

anya: i'll put together the sample patch for adapters and a migration timeline for private customers.

sam: thanks all. let's keep the probe non-blocking and conservative defaults so we don't cause customer-facing outages. close when RFC PR merged.
